clue.text: Lose old bet newly regarded as invalid

indicators.note: 'newly' suggests the letters are made over afresh into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
O is the standard abbreviation for old
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gambler loses an old wager that has since been declared void.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obsolete is out of date and no longer accepted as valid or in use.

clue.text: Hairdo worn by king beheading mother making meaningless speech

indicators.note: a hairdo worn by someone sits on top of them, so it comes first in the down entry
removing the head of a word means dropping its first letter

blocks.note: a bun is hair coiled into a knot
K is the chess abbreviation for king
MUM with its first letter cut off

explanation.surface: A monarch with a fancy hairdo executes his mother and talks nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunkum is nonsense, empty or insincere talk, so it fits meaningless speech as a synonym.

clue.text: Preserve headless nun in storage box

indicators.note: without a head means the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: to can food is to preserve it in tins
a nun is a SISTER, here missing its first letter

explanation.surface: Jam kept by a decapitated nun is put away in a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a round container, typically metal, used for keeping things such as tea or film.

clue.text: Animal clutching right bosom

indicators.note: something clutching another thing holds it inside its grip

blocks.note: a beast is an animal
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A creature grips the right side of someone's chest.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside BEAST to give BREAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosom and breast are synonyms for the chest, especially a woman's.

clue.text: Work in place for experiments by old university research leader

indicators.note: a leader is the one at the front, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: a lab, or laboratory, is where experiments happen
O is the abbreviation for old
U is the abbreviation for university
first letter of the word research

explanation.surface: Someone toils in a lab next to the retired head of research at a university.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour is a noun meaning work, especially hard physical effort, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Loved to keep end of chain joined up

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which is the one kept
to keep something is to hold on to it, so one part sits inside the other

blocks.note: liked is a milder form of loved
the last letter of chain

explanation.surface: Someone who adored a necklace keeps hold of its clasp end once it is fastened.
explanation.definitionFit: Linked means connected or joined together, as the links of a chain are.

clue.text: Moved swiftly to suppress source of tension and hostility

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter
to suppress something is to hold it down within, so one part is enclosed

blocks.note: hared means ran fast, like a hare
first letter of tension

explanation.surface: Someone acted quickly to dampen the strain and ill feeling in a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatred is intense dislike or enmity, which is a strong form of hostility.

clue.text: Ant and Dec swapping places to prepare a drink

indicators.note: the duo trade positions, so the second-named member is set down first

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The TV double act change sides on stage while mixing a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a British TV presenting duo, always billed in that order; putting Dec first gives DECANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To decant wine is to pour it carefully from the bottle into another vessel before serving it.

clue.text: Holy communion for cricketers?

blocks.note: the straight sense: the Christian sacrament commemorating the Last Supper
the setter's reading: an evening meal served at the famous London cricket ground

explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London ground known as the home of cricket, so a meal there would be the cricketers' evening spread.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord's Supper is a standard Christian name for the Eucharist, the service of Holy Communion.

clue.text: What to do before you 7 peacekeepers visit part of Ireland

blocks.note: the UN, or United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces
Cork is a county and city in Ireland

explanation.surface: United Nations troops on a tour of the Irish south coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 7-down: before you decant a wine you have to open the bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: You must pull the stopper from a bottle before pouring wine out of it, so this action precedes decanting.

clue.text: Crude oil given to government by principal member of ruling elite

indicators.note: crude means unrefined, so the letters are left in a rough, rearranged state
one thing given to another is attached to it, so the parts join in sequence

blocks.note: the word oil rearranged
G is the abbreviation for government
arch as a prefix means chief or principal, as in archbishop

explanation.surface: Unrefined petroleum is handed to the state by a powerful tycoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principal' looks like part of the definition but supplies ARCH, the prefix meaning chief.
explanation.definitionFit: An oligarch is one of a small group holding power, often a very rich business magnate.

clue.text: Lake is insignificant

blocks.note: first meaning: a small lake or pond, chiefly in poetic or place-name use
second meaning: being nothing more than, trifling

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a put-down of a small lake; in fact each word defines the answer on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a shallow lake, and as an adjective the word means small or trivial.

clue.text: Thinking seriously about intervening in dispute involving Tory leader

indicators.note: a leader stands at the front, so only the opening letter is used
involving means taking in, so one part is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: mediating is stepping in to settle a quarrel
first letter of Tory

explanation.surface: A politician ponders getting involved in a party quarrel concerning the Conservative chief.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party; its initial goes inside the word for peacemaking.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate on, or meditate, a plan is to consider it deeply, a form of serious reflection.

clue.text: Devil treats suspect to show

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

blocks.note: a demon is a devil
the word treats rearranged

explanation.surface: A demon gives a dodgy sweet to the audience at a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' reads as a verb, with 'Devil' doing the suspecting, but it is an adjective telling you to rearrange 'treats'.
explanation.definitionFit: To demonstrate is to prove or display something clearly, which matches the verb show.

clue.text: It's about actors being dull

blocks.note: over can mean concerning, as in a row over money
the cast is the set of actors in a production

explanation.surface: A complaint that a play is only about its performers, and they are boring.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcast sky is grey and cloudy, so the weather is dull.

clue.text: Put up with engineering role in gallery

indicators.note: engineering is construction work, so the letters are rebuilt into a new shape
in places one part inside the other

blocks.note: the Tate is a group of major British art galleries
the word role rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone endures an engineering job at an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ROLE goes after the first T of TATE, London's well-known gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate something is to endure or accept it, the same as to put up with it.

clue.text: Step round hot filament

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one part wraps about the other

blocks.note: a tread is a step or the horizontal part of a stair
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Instructions to walk around something burning, perhaps a glowing wire.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside TREAD after the T to give THREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A thread is a fine strand or fibre, which is what a filament is.

clue.text: Bird ingesting a dangerous substance

indicators.note: ingesting is swallowing, so one part ends up inside the other

blocks.note: a heron is a wading bird
I is one, which a can mean

explanation.surface: A bird swallows something toxic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' becomes I, as both can mean one.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroin is an addictive opioid drug, a substance that is harmful and potentially lethal.

clue.text: Butcher could be adulterating pork with European sheep

indicators.note: adulterating means contaminating, so the mixture is spoiled and its letters jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for European
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dishonest butcher might pass off pork padded out with imported mutton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher' looks like the anagram signal, but it starts the definition; the mixing word is 'adulterating'.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher runs a shop selling meat, so he is one example of a retailer.

clue.text: Posit a new variety of language

indicators.note: something new is made differently, so the letters take a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A linguist proposes that a new dialect exists.
explanation.definitionFit: A patois is a regional dialect, often a non-standard variety spoken by ordinary people.

clue.text: Send up note to get ingredient for cheesemaking

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending a word up writes it from the bottom, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: a tenner is a ten-pound banknote

explanation.surface: Someone posts a written note to order a key item for making cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' is money, not a message or a musical note: a British ten-pound note is a tenner, which upwards gives RENNET.
explanation.definitionFit: Rennet is the enzyme preparation used to curdle milk, an essential ingredient in making cheese.

clue.text: Ship over a vegetable

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word is read the other way

blocks.note: the keel stands for the whole ship by synecdoche, as a keel is a ship's backbone

explanation.surface: A cargo of vegetables is sent across by boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Keel is a poetic word for a ship, from its backbone timber.
explanation.definitionFit: The leek is an onion-family vegetable with a long white stem, the national emblem of Wales.

clue.text: Flexible growth found in cattle ranging freely over space

indicators.note: animals ranging freely wander anywhere, so these letters roam out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
an en is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: A strange bendy outgrowth turns up on free-range cattle grazing over open country.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printer's space half the width of an em, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A tentacle is a long flexible limb or organ growing from an animal such as an octopus.

clue.text: Rushed back to join queue to get slim

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word is read from its end
joining means attaching, so the two parts are placed side by side

blocks.note: ran means hurried; it is then read the other way
a row is a line of people or things

explanation.surface: Someone hurried back to a line, hoping to lose weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow means of small width, so it matches slim as a near synonym for thin.

clue.text: Red is fermented with last bit of yeast to become the most sec

indicators.note: fermenting changes a liquid chemically, so these letters are transformed into a new order
the last bit of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of yeast

explanation.surface: Red wine fermented with yeast ends up as the driest of all.
explanation.walkthrough: Sec is the French word for dry, used on wine labels.
explanation.definitionFit: Sec describes wine that is dry, so the most sec is the superlative of dry.

clue.text: Went crazy working with physicist

indicators.note: crazy means mad, so the letters go wild and rearrange

blocks.note: the word went rearranged
on means operating, as in a machine that is on

explanation.surface: Someone lost their mind collaborating with a scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton was the English scientist who formulated the laws of motion and gravity.
